title: How many cherry-picking sequences are needed to reduce all subtrees of a phylogenetic tree?
summary: Phylogenetic networks are graphs that represent the evolutionary history of species. Recently, the class of orchard phylogenetic networks, which can be reduced by so-called cherry-picking sequences, has gained attention for its computational and biological aspects. In this paper, we study a fundamental question on orchards and their cherry-picking sequences by considering the CoveringNumber problem: given an orchard network $N$, how many cherry-picking sequences are needed to reduce all subnetworks of $N$?
